title: B1-10 · The tamyīz and the absolute complement

blocks.text: B1-10 · The tamyīz and the absolute complement
Lesson overview

Two charges still, both very frequent in the language of information. The tamyīz ( ⁧التَّمْيِيز⁩ , "Specification" is precise with respect to what a quantity or comparison is worth: ⁧عِشْرُونَ كِتَابًا⁩ , ⁧أَكْثَرُ أَهَمِّيَّةً⁩ More importantly, ⁧اِزْدَادَ الوَضْعُ سُوءًا⁩ The situation has deteriorated. Thanks to tamyīz You can compare any adjective, even those that have no form. ⁧أَفْعَل⁩ . The absolute complement ( ⁧المَفْعُولُ المُطْلَقُ⁩ ) repeats maṣdar of the verb to say how or how much the action took place: ⁧اِرْتَفَعَتِ الأَسْعَارُ ارْتِفَاعًا كَبِيرًا⁩ The prices have increased significantly, ⁧شَكَرْتُهُ شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا⁩ . Two weeks.

rows: 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 115–116), plus the EGY track

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Grammar G50, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. use the tamyīz after the numbers from 11 a 99 and after ⁧كَمْ⁩ question;
2. make the comparative and superlative of each adjective with ⁧أَكْثَرُ⁩ / ⁧أَقَلُّ⁩ / ⁧أَشَدُّ⁩ + tamyīz;
3. use the tamyīz with the verbs of increase and decrease ( ⁧اِزْدَادَ⁩ , ⁧تَضَاعَفَ⁩ ) and measures;
4. recognize and use the absolute complement with an adjective, iḍāfa and to indicate the number of times;
5. recognise absolute complements ⁧شُكْرًا⁩ , ⁧طَبْعًا⁩ , ⁧جِدًّا⁩ , ⁧أَيْضًا⁩ );
6. translating tamyīz and absolute complement with natural Italian adverbs and complements.
Two-week plan.

blocks.text: 1. Dialogue 1 · What flight?
Luca and Hudā compare flights to Cairo in July.

rows: Hudā: How many flights have you found?
⁧ثَلَاثَ رِحْلَاتٍ. الأُولَى مُبَاشِرَةٌ، وَالثَّانِيَةُ وَالثَّالِثَةُ عَبْرَ إِسْطَنْبُولَ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧وَأَثِينَا.⁩
Three flights. The first is directed, the second and third via Istanbul and Athens.
⁧المُبَاشِرَةُ أَقْصَرُ مُدَّةً طَبْعًا. وَكَمْ سَاعَةً تَسْتَغْرِقُ؟⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩
Hudā: Direct is shorter, of course. And how many hours does it last?
⁧ثَلَاثَ سَاعَاتٍ وَنِصْفًا. لٰكِنَّهَا أَغْلَى سِعْرًا: ثَلَاثُمِئَةٍ وَعِشْرُونَ يُورُو.⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩
Three and a half hours. But it costs more: three hundred twenty euros.
Hudā: What about that one via Istanbul?
⁧أَرْخَصُ بِكَثِيرٍ، وَلٰكِنَّهَا أَطْوَلُ: إِحْدَى عَشْرَةَ سَاعَةً تَقْرِيبًا، مَعَ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧تَوَقُّفٍ سَبْعَ سَاعَاتٍ فِي المَطَارِ!⁩
Luca: It costs much less, but it is longer: about eleven hours, with a seven-hour airport stopover!
⁧لَا، هٰذَا أَكْثَرُ تَعَبًا مِنَ العَمَلِ اللَّيْلِيِّ! وَأَثِينَا؟⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩
Hudā: No, it's more tiring than the night shift! What about Athens?
⁧سِتُّ سَاعَاتٍ، وَالسِّعْرُ مُتَوَسِّطٌ. لٰكِنَّ الشَّرِكَةَ أَقَلُّ شُهْرَةً، وَلَا⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧أَعْرِفُ جَوْدَةَ خِدْمَاتِهَا.⁩
Luca: Six hours, and the price is average. But the company is less known, and I don't know what the quality of service is like.
⁧خُذِ المُبَاشِرَةَ. صَحِيحٌ أَنَّهَا أَكْثَرُ تَكْلِفَةً، لٰكِنَّهَا أَكْثَرُ⁩ : ⁧نَصِيحَتِي⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧رَاحَةً، وَسَتَصِلُ أَقَلَّ تَعَبًا.⁩
Hudā: My advice: take direct. True, it costs more, but it's more comfortable and you'll get less tired.
⁧مَعَكِ حَقٌّ. سَأَحْجِزُهَا اللَّيْلَةَ، قَبْلَ أَنْ تَزْدَادَ الأَسْعَارُ ارْتِفَاعًا!⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩
You're right. I'll book it tonight before the prices go up again!

2. What is the tamyīz

The tamyīz is an indefinite name to the accusative that removes ambiguity to a previous word: a number, a measure, a comparison, a verb of increase. Answers the question: "How much of what?" or "more in what?"
⁧اِزْدَادَ⁩ ... (increased in what?) ⁧اِزْدَادَ عَدَدًا⁩ is increased in number
3. The tamyīz Numbers and ⁧كَمْ⁩

Numbers from 11 a 99: singular indeterminate accusation. ⁧أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كِتَابًا⁩ , ⁧عِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا⁩ , ⁧خَمْسٌ وَتِسْعُونَ سَنَةً⁩ . (Remember: from 3 a 10 plural genitive, ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ كُتُبٍ⁩ ; 100 and 1000 singular genitive, ⁧مِئَةُ كِتَابٍ⁩ . The whole system in B1-13.) ⁧كَمْ⁩ question: singular accusative. ⁧كَمْ كِتَابًا قَرَأْتَ؟⁩ How many books have you read? ⁧كَمْ سَنَةً عِشْتَ فِي مِصْرَ؟⁩ How many years have you lived in Egypt? With a preposition in front there is also the genitive: ⁧بِكَمْ دِينَارٍ؟⁩ For how many dinars? Watch your mouth. In conversation many say ⁧كَمْ كِتَاب⁩ without desinence; in the writing always put the accusative ( ⁧كَمْ كِتَابًا⁩ ).
4. The comparison with the tamyīz

Many adjectives do not have the form ⁧أَفْعَل⁩ : those of derived forms ( ⁧مُهِمّ⁩ , ⁧مُرِيح⁩ , ⁧مُعَقَّد⁩ ), colors, nisba ( ⁧اِقْتِصَادِيّ⁩ ). For comparative and superlative use ⁧أَكْثَرُ⁩ / ⁧أَقَلُّ⁩ / ⁧أَشَدُّ⁩ + maṣdar or abstract name to the accusative.
⁧أَقَلُّ شُهْرَةًمَشْهُور⁩ less famous

The superlative uses the same pattern with the article or in iḍāfa: ⁧المَدِينَةُ الأَكْثَرُ تَلَوُّثًا⁩ The most polluted city is: ⁧أَكْثَرُ المُدُنِ تَلَوُّثًا⁩ It is the most polluted of cities. In newspapers form with the article ( ⁧الأَكْثَرُ⁩ + tamyīz) is very frequent. ( ⁧تَلَوُّث⁩ • pollution • • even with ⁧أَفْعَل⁩ direct on tamyīz specify the comparison: ⁧أَكْبَرُ سِنًّا⁩ • older than age • ⁧أَحْسَنُ حَالًا⁩ In better condition. ⁧أَقْصَرُ مُدَّةً⁩ Shorter duration of the period (s)
5. The tamyīz with verbs and measures
Verbs of increase and decrease: ⁧اِزْدَادَ⁩ Increment: ⁧تَضَاعَفَ⁩ • double • double • ⁧كَثُرَ⁩ , ⁧قَلَّ⁩ .
⁧اِزْدَادَ الوَضْعُ سُوءًا.⁩ The situation has worsened (Lett. is increased in malice).

rows: The city has become even more beautiful.

blocks.text: ⁧تَضَاعَفَ الزُّوَّارُ عَدَدًا.⁩ · ⁧تَضَاعَفَ عَدَدُ الزُّوَّارِ.⁩ The number of visitors has doubled.

Measures. In the classical language: ⁧عِنْدِي كِيلُو لَحْمًا⁩ , ⁧شَرِبْتُ كُوبًا مَاءً⁩ . In the modern language you prefer ⁧مِنْ⁩ : ⁧كِيلُو مِنَ اللَّحْمِ⁩ , ⁧كُوبٌ مِنَ المَاءِ⁩ or theiḍāfa: ⁧كُوبُ مَاءٍ⁩ . Recognize the classic form.
6. Dialogue 2 · The mid-year interview
Salmā meets each student for a progress report. It's Luca's turn.

rows: ⁧تَفَضَّلْ يَا لُوكَا. قَرَأْتُ امْتِحَانَكَ قِرَاءَةً دَقِيقَةً.⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩
Salmā: Sit down, Luca. I read your test carefully.
What do you think? I'm a little worried.
⁧لَا دَاعِيَ لِلْقَلَقِ! تَحَسَّنَ مُسْتَوَاكَ تَحَسُّنًا كَبِيرًا، خُصُوصًا فِي⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧القِرَاءَةِ.⁩
Salmā: There is no reason to worry! Your level has improved a lot, especially in reading.
Luca: Thank God! What about the writing?
⁧الأَسْعَارُ⁩ » ⁧جَيِّدَةٌ، لٰكِنَّكَ تُخْطِئُ أَحْيَانًا فِي المُطَابَقَةِ. كَتَبْتَ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ! ⁧مَرَّتَيْنِ⁩ « ⁧ارْتَفَعُوا⁩
Salmā: Good, but sometimes you miss the deal. You wrote the prices went up with the male plural twice!
Luke: (laughs) I know, he even corrected it. Laylā.
⁧وَفِي المُحَادَثَةِ تَتَكَلَّمُ بِثِقَةٍ، لٰكِنْ يَجِبُ أَنْ تَسْتَمِعَ اسْتِمَاعًا أَكْثَرَ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧تَرْكِيزًا. أَحْيَانًا تُجِيبُ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَفْهَمَ السُّؤَالَ.⁩
Salmā: In the conversation, you talk with confidence, but you have to listen more focused. Sometimes you answer before you understand the question.
Luca: It's also my habit at work!
⁧إِذَنْ اسْتَعِدَّ لِلْقَاهِرَةِ اسْتِعْدَادًا جَيِّدًا: هُنَاكَ النَّاسُ يَتَكَلَّمُونَ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧بِسُرْعَةٍ وَلَا يَنْتَظِرُونَ أَحَدًا.⁩
Salmā: Then prepare well for Cairo: people talk fast there and wait for no one.
⁧شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا يَا أُسْتَاذَةُ. أَشْكُرُكِ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شُكْرًا كَبِيرًا.⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩
Thank you very much, Professor. Thank you so much for everything.

blocks.text: ⁧مَنِ الطَّالِبُ التَّالِي؟⁩ … ⁧لَا شُكْرَ عَلَى وَاجِبٍ. وَالآنَ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: You're welcome, it's my duty. And now... who's next?

What to notice. Absolute complements: ⁧قَرَأْتُ⁩ … ⁧قِرَاءَةً دَقِيقَةً⁩ I have read carefully. ⁧تَحَسَّنَ⁩ … ⁧تَحَسُّنًا كَبِيرًا⁩ It has improved very much, ⁧تَسْتَمِعَ اسْتِمَاعًا أَكْثَرَ تَرْكِيزًا⁩ • to listen with more focus (with a tamyīz Inside), ⁧اِسْتَعِدَّ⁩ … ⁧اسْتِعْدَادًا جَيِّدًا⁩ Manufacture in which the value of all the materials used does not exceed 50% of the ex-works price of the product ⁧أَشْكُرُكِ⁩ … ⁧شُكْرًا كَبِيرًا⁩ . Fossils: ⁧شُكْرًا⁩ , ⁧جِدًّا⁩ , ⁧أَحْيَانًا⁩ , ⁧خُصُوصًا. لَا دَاعِيَ لِـ⁩ There is no reason to do this. ⁧تُخْطِئُ⁩ (IV of ⁧خ ط أ⁩ ). ⁧بِثِقَةٍ⁩ With security. ⁧عَادَة⁩ - It's a habit. ⁧لَا شُكْرَ عَلَى وَاجِبٍ⁩ There is no need to thank for a duty: formal response to thanks. ⁧التَّالِي⁩ The next one, the following.
7. The absolute complement
The absolute complement is the maṣdar of the same verb to the accusative. It strengthens itself (it really does, it does); with an adjective, aiḍāfa or a number says how or how many times.
alone (emphasis) ⁧رَفَضَ رَفْضًا.⁩ He refused categorically.

The maṣdar Right. The absolute complement uses the maṣdar of the verb, in the same form: ⁧اِرْتَفَعَ⁩ ( VIII) → ⁧اِرْتِفَاعًا⁩ , ⁧تَحَسَّنَ⁩ ( V) → ⁧تَحَسُّنًا⁩ , ⁧رَحَّبَ⁩ (II) → ⁧تَرْحِيبًا⁩ . There is also a maṣdar of a verb near: ⁧جَلَسَ قُعُودًا⁩ ; and sometimes a substitute as ⁧كُلّ⁩ / ⁧بَعْض⁩ / ⁧أَيّ⁩ in iḍāfa: ⁧لَا أَعْرِفُهُ أَيَّ مَعْرِفَةٍ⁩ I don't know him at all. In newspapers the absolute complement with an adjective is a fixed formula: ⁧اِنْخَفَضَ انْخِفَاضًا طَفِيفًا⁩ It is slightly lowered, ⁧اِرْتَفَعَ ارْتِفَاعًا حَادًّا⁩ It has climbed abruptly, ⁧تَرَاجَعَ تَرَاجُعًا مَلْحُوظًا⁩ • has dropped significantly, ⁧تَحَسَّنَ تَحَسُّنًا تَدْرِيجِيًّا⁩ It has gradually improved.
8. The absolute complements are "fossil"
Many words in -an that you have been using for years are absolute complements that have lost the verb:
9. Translate
⁧أَكْثَرُ أَهَمِّيَّةً⁩ more important (no longer of importance)
The golden rule: the absolute complement with an adjective almost always becomes an Italian adverb; on tamyīz after a comparison disappears into the Italian adjective.
10. Pronunciation

The indeterminate prosecutor. ʿišrūna kitāban, akṯaru ahammiyyatan, irtifāʿan kabīran: the -an must be heard within the sentence. Pause (end of sentence) becomes -ā: …irtifāʿan kabīrā. Long groups. akṯaru ahammiyyatan, ašaddu ḫuṭūratan: read in one comparative breath + tamyīz, without pause in the middle.
11. New lexicon
★ ⁧مُعَقَّد⁩ muʿaqqad complicated ⁧ع ق د⁩ passive participle ⁧تَعْقِيد⁩ Complicated (II)
★ ⁧قِيَاسِيّ⁩ qiyāsiyy record ⁧ق ي س⁩ adjective ⁧رَقْمٌ قِيَاسِيٌّ⁩ A record

Notes of use. ⁧اِزْدَادَ⁩ is the form VIII of ⁧ز ي د⁩ with assimilation ⁧ت⁩ → ⁧د⁩ after ⁧ز⁩ (as ⁧اِزْدَحَمَ⁩ It is crowded, from which ⁧اِزْدِحَام⁩ , B1-04). ⁧بَالِغ⁩ in iḍāfa with an abstract name is an elegant way of intensifying: ⁧بَالِغُ الخُطُورَةِ⁩ Very serious, ⁧بَالِغُ الأَهَمِّيَّةِ⁩ It's very important. ⁧مَلْحُوظ⁩ and ⁧طَفِيف⁩ are the two adjectives most used by the news to say "very much" and "little" in variations.

13. Exercises
Exercise 1 · Numbers and ⁧كَمْ⁩

Complete with the tamyīz in the right form: a) ⁧قَرَأْتُ عِشْرِينَ ◌⁩ ( ⁧كِتَاب⁩ ). · b) ⁧فِي الصَّفِّ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ ◌⁩ ( ⁧طَالِب⁩ ). · c) ⁧كَمْ ◌⁩ ( ⁧سَاعَة⁩ ) ⁧تَعْمَلُ فِي الأُسْبُوعِ؟⁩ · d) ⁧اِنْتَظَرْنَا أَرْبَعِينَ ◌⁩ ( ⁧دَقِيقَة⁩ ). · e) ⁧كَمْ ◌⁩ ( ⁧لُغَة⁩ ) ⁧تَتَكَلَّمِينَ؟⁩ · f) ⁧عُمْرُهُ سِتُّونَ ◌⁩ ( ⁧سَنَة⁩ ).
Exercise 2 · Comparatives with the tamyīz

Make the comparison: a) ⁧هٰذَا الدَّرْسُ مُهِمٌّ⁩ (← more important than the previous one) · b) ⁧هٰذِهِ الشَّقَّةُ مُرِيحَةٌ⁩ (← more comfortable than the old) · c) ⁧المَسْأَلَةُ مُعَقَّدَةٌ⁩ (← more complicated than yesterday) · d) ⁧الطَّرِيقُ خَطِيرٌ⁩ (← more dangerous at night) · e) ⁧هٰذَا الكَاتِبُ مَشْهُورٌ⁩ (← less famous than his brother) · f) ⁧هٰذِهِ المَدِينَةُ جَمِيلَةٌ⁩ (← the most beautiful city in the country, with ⁧الأَكْثَر⁩ )
Exercise 3 · Verbs of increase

Translate with ⁧اِزْدَادَ⁩ or ⁧تَضَاعَفَ⁩ + tamyīz: a) The situation has worsened. · b) The number of tourists has doubled. · c) The problem has become more complicated. · d) The city has become even more beautiful. · e) Prices have risen again. · f) Time has become colder ( ⁧بَرْدًا⁩ ).
Exercise 4 · The absolute complement with the adjective
